findings.description: _read_all() catches OSError, ValueError and KeyError and returns an empty dict. A transient read failure (permissions, I/O error, a partially written or corrupt file) is therefore indistinguishable from 'no sessions'. The following save() or delete() calls read {}, add or remove one record, and _write_all() overwrites the file with that single record. Every other user's live sessions are silently lost and those users are logged out. The same empty result makes take_by_refresh() return None, so valid refresh tokens are rejected.
findings.suggestion: Only treat a missing file (FileNotFoundError) as an empty store. Let other OSError and ValueError/KeyError propagate, or raise StoreError, so that writes never run on data that was not read successfully.
findings.title: Unreadable or corrupt session file is treated as empty, so the next write wipes every session

findings.description: sign_out_everywhere() catches StoreError from store.delete(), logs a warning, and continues. The session remains usable, and its access token still passes authenticate(). change_password() returns this count as if the sessions had been ended, and callers have no way to know some sessions survived. After a password reset, an attacker holding a stolen session can keep access even though the caller believes all sessions were ended.
findings.suggestion: Do not swallow the error. Let StoreError propagate so the caller fails the request, or collect the failures and raise after attempting the rest, so that change_password can report incomplete revocation.
findings.title: Failed session revocation is logged and skipped, so sessions stay valid after sign-out or password change

findings.description: The Session dataclass is removed and login() now returns IssuedSession, which has access_token and refresh_token instead of token. The constructor's second positional argument changes from ttl to store, so existing calls such as SessionManager(users, ttl) now pass a timedelta as the store. Callers that read session.token or pass ttl will fail at runtime, and the failure may only appear on the login path.
findings.suggestion: Keep a token attribute or a compatibility alias for callers that still need it, or update every caller in the same change and note the breaking change explicitly.
findings.title: SessionManager constructor and login return type changed in a breaking way
